request: User (13 Oct 2026) shared a Living screenshot of the 3D walkthrough and a generated Bedroom 2 ideation image: the 3D render should have real material texture so it shows how the house will look in reality, not a flat college-project look.
sources_used: User screenshot of Living viewpoint (13 Oct 2026)
User-supplied generated Bedroom 2 ideation image (13 Oct 2026)
output/jaipur-home/model/interior.js (materials lines 1-67, lights lines 68-76; three.js r160)
audit_findings: Renderer already has ACES tone mapping, PCF soft shadows, one sun, per-room point lights and a neutral PMREM studio environment.
Textures are 512 px procedural canvases (oak, tile, granite, fabric, bath). Walls, laminates, rug, paint have no texture at all.
No normal, roughness or bump maps anywhere; every surface has uniform roughness, so nothing catches light.
No ambient occlusion or bounced light: corners, sofa bases, wardrobe-to-floor joints do not darken.
Square-edged boxes everywhere; real joinery has 2-3 mm edge radii that catch highlights.
Living screenshot shows a dark navy rectangle above the passage (looks like scene background showing through a ceiling gap); to be investigated, not assumed.
geometry_policy: No change to walls, columns, openings, room sizes, fixture or furniture dimensions, colliders or positions. Edge radii, if approved, stay inside existing bounding boxes.

options.A: Realtime PBR upgrade of walkthrough.html: 1024-2048 px procedural albedo/normal/roughness maps in world-scale UVs (veneer grain, vitrified tile with grout, plaster, linen weave, granite), warm window/ceiling light, ambient occlusion pass with a Standard/High toggle, small edge radii. Works offline; GLB gets the same maps.
options.B: Offline path-traced stills (Blender Cycles from the GLB, CPU only, minutes per image) for the key viewpoints. Photographic light bounce and soft shadows, but stills not a walkable model. Needs the same material work as A.
options.C: A then B: materials first, stills second.

recommendation: C, starting with A. B reuses A's materials, so A first costs nothing extra.
limits_to_state_honestly: Browser realtime PBR will look like good architectural visualisation, not a photograph. The generated ideation images stay more photographic.
Materials shown are design intent. Real veneer, tile and fabric selections need physical samples (RFI-001/003 style site checks), not a render.
risks_and_dependencies: Ambient occlusion and larger textures cost frame rate on weak laptops; Standard mode keeps current performance.
walkthrough.html grows (currently 868 KB) and GLB grows (currently 7.7 MB) with embedded maps.
Defect fixes D1-D8 from the fresh-context review are a separate revision to avoid mixing visual and geometric changes.
validation_plan: Scripted check that fixtures, furniture and colliders are identical to baseline R-007.
Before/after captures of Living, Master, Bedroom 2, Bedroom 3, Kitchen.
Frame-time check in headless Chromium for Standard and High.
Independent QA via router when available; otherwise labelled fresh-context review.

scope_approval.note: Route A then B (realtime PBR first, path-traced stills second); 2-3 mm edge radii on joinery/furniture approved within existing bounding boxes.

results: verification/verify-geometry.json: 1920 meshes, max bbox delta 0 ft, fixtures/furniture/colliders/viewpoints identical
